Today’s sophisticated AI models create synthetic voices that sound like natural speech. Trained on huge datasets of real human voices, these models use advanced neural networks to identify and replicate authentic speech patterns. Creating a synthetic voice is also called speech synthesis or voice synthesis, while the audio it produces is called synthetic speech.

To create a new synthetic voice, a user records themselves talking. Meanwhile, the AI model analyzes their unique phonetic patterns and inflection and uses this data to replicate their voice. Then, the user can adjust vocal characteristics like accent, tone, and pacing to create the final product. Some synthetic voices are a direct clone of one person’s speech, while others are a blend of multiple voices. Voices can also be designed from a text description , with no recording at all.

Synthetic voices open up a wide range of creative possibilities for podcasts, audiobooks, video games, and advertising. In this article, we’ll explore how synthetic voices are created, what makes them sound natural, and how to build your own synthetic voice with ElevenLabs.

## Summary

• Synthetic voices are created with neural AI models that analyze and replicate human speech patterns.

• Synthetic voices are helpful for narrating audiobooks, generating video game dialogue, creating podcasts and voiceovers at scale, creating customer service AI agents , or even preserving voices that are at risk.

• Voice cloning works by analyzing recordings of a specific person’s voice and replicating their unique accent and speech patterns.

• Modern AI voices sound natural because they replicate human prosody and are context-aware, instead of just replicating individual words or syllables.

## How synthetic voices are created, step by step

Synthetic voice creation is a three-step process.

Here’s what that looks like in practice:

• Step 1: Collect voice data: Synthetic voices start with real human speech. To create a new voice, you’ll need audio recordings of the speakers you want to replicate. The more data you provide, the more accurate and realistic the final voice will be. Here are some best practices for voice cloning .

• Step 2: Train or fine-tune an AI model: To create synthetic voices, AI models first analyze extensive datasets with a diverse range of speech recordings. The models use this data to understand human speech patterns. After an AI model has been trained, it can clone real-life voices using a single speech recording. In most cases, you’ll be using a pre-trained model rather than building your own from scratch.

• Step 3: Generate audio from text: Synthetic voices use text to speech to generate audio. You can adjust factors like speed and tone to match your preferences. For a deeper look, read our guide to how text to speech technology works .

## From speech data to neural text to speech

Neural text to speech models are trained on numerous datasets of real speech recordings. This dataset includes recordings with different languages, accents, emotions, and pitch levels. Neural text to speech is a widely used form of speech synthesis today.

Traditional models stitched together existing recordings of words, syllables, and phonemes . The results were very robotic, as they couldn’t replicate the variations in pitch, rhythm, and expression that make speech sound human.

Instead of just learning how letters and syllables sound, modern neural text to speech models learn natural human pronunciation patterns and speech rhythms. When converting text to speech, these models assess the text, convert it into acoustic features, then use those features to generate waveforms.

Since acoustic features like pitch, rhythm, and tone are built into neural AI models, the resulting speech sounds much more natural and authentic than the models of the past.

The results are also customizable: you can change factors like speed, emotion, and even accent to get the exact voice you’re looking for. For example, your brand could use the same synthetic voice across your website but use excitement and urgency for marketing content and calmness for customer service interactions.

## Standard, neural, and generative text to speech

Text to speech models fall into three broad generations.

Understanding the differences between them helps contextualize why modern models, like ElevenLabs Text to Speech, can sound so natural.

• Standard text to speech: These systems stitch together prerecorded sounds or follow rules and statistical models to pronounce text. The output is understandable but robotic, with limited emotion.

• Neural text to speech: Deep learning models learn pronunciation, rhythm, and intonation from large sets of recordings, and generate speech that sounds far more natural and consistent.

• Generative text to speech: Generative models are trained on even larger and more varied speech data, and they use the meaning of the text to decide emotion, pacing, and emphasis. You can steer their delivery with instructions, such as audio tags .

Modern voice platforms rely on neural and generative models, while standard text to speech mostly survives in legacy systems.

## What makes AI voice generation sound natural?

Synthetic voices generated by AI sound very similar to human voices. In fact, it can be challenging to tell the difference between them if you’re not listening closely.

There are two reasons why AI-generated voices sound more natural than the robotic voices of the past: prosody and context awareness.

## Prosody

Prosody is the rhythm of natural human speech. Small changes in intonation and speed convey tone and emotion as we talk. For example, speaking quickly might convey stress or excitement, while raising your pitch at the end of a sentence turns a statement into a question.
